name: Template: humanitarian relief in crises
summary: TEMPLATE: what the charity does, in which crises, the year modelled, the bottom line in years of healthy life per $1,000 (quote it live in the write-up), and the biggest uncertainty. If the result is more than ten times its cause's median on the site, say why ("more than ten times its peers because …").

source.title: charityevals' estimate: humanitarian relief in crises

sections.title: Cost
sections.explainer: What the modelled program cost in the year the outcomes below are counted for, including its share of overhead. From audited financial statements or the annual report.

sections.title: Reach
sections.explainer: How many people, animals or meals the spending reached in the same year, as the charity reports it.

sections.title: Effect per unit
sections.explainer: What the intervention does for each unit reached, from the best available studies, before any adjustment.

sections.title: Adjustments
sections.explainer: Discounts for weaker evidence, what would have happened anyway, credit shared with others, and delivery falling short. All multiply the outcome.

sections.title: Other outcomes, in this model's unit
sections.explainer: charityevals' standard step for outcomes in more than one unit (docs/normalization.md 2.6): each outcome is counted in its own unit (units of value for income and deaths, WELLBYs for life satisfaction, tonnes of CO₂e, chicken pain days) and put into this model's unit by its unit's conversion over this unit's, which the headline's conversion cancels. So each moves only with its own sliders, exactly as in a model of its own unit. The rows are fixed; don't edit them.

sections.title: Outcome
sections.explainer: The outcome in the family's shared unit, per dollar.

sections.title: Your dollar's share
sections.explainer: Staff who earn less than they could elsewhere pay part of the cost in kind. With credit by share of resources, your dollar is credited with its share of the full cost only.

rows.label: Spending on the modelled program(s) in the year modelled

rows.label: ln(consumption) gain per person
rows.explainer: A year's goods on the site's one log-income scale.

rows.label: Evidence adjustment (internal and external validity), a multiplier
rows.explainer: TEMPLATE: how far the effect size above should be trusted for this charity's setting: publication bias, self-report bias, replication, differences between study populations and this program. A multiplier (1 = take the studies at face value), the product of its parts; say each part, its anchor (the same adjustment in another model of this intervention) and the range.

rows.label: Share of the outcome other responders wouldn't have delivered
rows.explainer: TEMPLATE: how much of this response would have been delivered anyway by the government, UN agencies or other NGOs had this charity not been there: from the response's funding coverage (OCHA FTS, the appeal's percentage funded) and gaps in the cluster's 4W data. Name the source.

rows.label: This charity's share of the resources behind the outcome
rows.explainer: TEMPLATE: where other organisations contributed to the same outcome (co-funders, coalition campaigns, government delivery), this charity's share of everyone's spending on it. Others' in-kind work counts too: government staff time, partners' own delivery costs, and volunteers' unpaid time (beyond any stipend the charity pays, which is in its cost), valued at the local wage for the hours given. 1 when it delivers alone.

rows.label: Share of credit used
rows.explainer: The charity's share of the resources behind the outcome; it applies whichever way credit is shared.

rows.label: Delivery adjustment (fidelity, compliance, follow-through)
rows.explainer: TEMPLATE: the share of the reported reach that actually receives the intervention as studied: dose completion, coverage survey vs. reported.

rows.label: Leverage and funging
rows.explainer: TEMPLATE: below 1 when other funders (governments, the Global Fund) would have paid for this work without the donation; above 1 when the donation pulls in other money. GiveWell's top charities typically sit at 0.85–0.95.

rows.label: Counted less where the outcome isn't measured for this charity
rows.explainer: TEMPLATE: the shared missing-data step (docs/normalization.md 2.12). Keep $missing_data_discount when this branch's outcome rests on the research literature or on judgment rather than on this charity's own data: reach that is a judgment (spending over an assumed cost per person, no count of its own), an effect that is a judgment, or a programme with no outcome data built from the literature on its kind of work. Set the formula to 1 only when the charity's own count of who got the intervention meets an effect measured with a credible counterfactual (its own controlled evaluation, or trials of the same intervention delivered the same way, dose and population), and say which here.

rows.label: All adjustments combined
rows.formula: evidence_adj * counterfactual_adj * attribution_share * implementation_adj * leverage_funging_adj * missing_data_adj
rows.explainer: The product of the adjustments above.

rows.label: Benefits and harms not modelled, as a share of modelled value
rows.explainer: TEMPLATE: a supplementary adjustment: list each effect not modelled with its sign and size. Benefits are positive shares, harms and risks (funging inside the organisation, bottlenecks, monitoring errors) negative shares of value lost, added here: never a positive share subtracted elsewhere.
